title: Tiered Access Attestation and Archival Playbook
author: Sofia Patel
doc_body:
Summary:
This playbook defines Redwood Inference's operational approach for tiered access attestation, archival of authorization evidence, and associated audit-log retention across jurisdictions. It describes role tiers and attestation cadence, the packaging format for compliance evidence, retention and archival rules per data residency policy, and the triggers that elevate risk to the exceptions workflow. Intended audience: security engineers, compliance owners, SREs, and platform owners who operate identity, access, and logging systems.

Purpose and scope:
- Provide a repeatable attestation cadence for all production access roles (human and service identities).
- Define the archival format and locations for authorization evidence used for audits (SOC2, ISO, customer audits).
- Map retention windows and legal hold behavior by geography and data sensitivity class.
- Integrate with incident response for access-related incidents and exceptions.

Audience and owner:
- Primary audience: Security team, Compliance, Eng-SRE, and Platform (IAM) owners.
- Document owner: security (Sofia Patel).
- Operational contacts: Marcus Liu (IAM), Evelyn Reed (Compliance), Diego Morales (Audit Logging).

Key definitions (short):
- Tiered roles: Role grouping based on privilege and risk (Tier 0 = org admins, Tier 1 = service operators, Tier 2 = normal engineers, Tier 3 = read-only non-prod).
- Attestation: periodic confirmation by role owners that access assignments are still valid.
- Authorization evidence bundle (AEB): packaged artifact containing role membership snapshots, delegated policies, and related audit logs for a given period.
- Archival store: long-term encrypted storage (S3 buckets with restricted KMS keys or on-prem vault archive) where evidence is immutable.

Principles:
1) Least privilege by default; explicit, documented exceptions required for deviations.
2) Evidence must be tamper-evident and reproducible (signed manifests + hash).
3) Retention must satisfy the strictest applicable jurisdictional requirement when data crosses borders.
4) Attestation cadence increases with role tier and prior exceptions.

Role tiers and attestation cadence:
- Tier 0 (Org Admins, Org-level owners): attestation every 30 days. Manual verification required; two approvers.
- Tier 1 (Service owners, Privileged operators): attestation every 90 days. One technical lead + one compliance reviewer.
- Tier 2 (Engineers with write access to production resources): attestation every 180 days. Automated reminders, delegated attestation supported.
- Tier 3 (Read-only, dev/test): attestation annually.
- Elevated/Exception roles: ad-hoc attestation at time of exception plus follow-up 30 days after remediation.

Attestation workflow (high level):
1) IAM system extracts role membership snapshot and policy attachments for the attestation window (example command below).
2) Automated email and Slack reminders to role owners with a link to the attestation UI.
3) Owner reviews membership, marks Approve or selects entries for removal, attaching justification where needed.
4) Approvals generate an Authorization Evidence Bundle (AEB) and checksum manifest. The AEB is signed by the attestation service using a rotation-protected key.
5) AEB archived per retention policy; audit log entries are retained and associated with bundle ID.

IAM extraction example (pseudo-CLI):
- Command: redwood-iam snapshot --role "prod-service-ops" --window 2026-07-01:2026-07-31 --format json > prod-service-ops-2026-07.json
- Included fields: role_id, member_principal (user/service), membership_start, membership_end (if any), policy_arn, attached_permissions, attested_by, attestation_timestamp

Authorization Evidence Bundle (AEB) specification:
- File layout (tar.gz):
  - metadata.json (manifest with bundle_id, attestation_window, created_by, signature, checksum)
  - roles/ (role snapshots as role-<role_id>.json)
  - policies/ (policy text files or links to policy version IDs)
  - logs/ (minimally required audit log slices; see Log slices below)
  - proofs/ (signature files, KMS key ID, hash chain entries)
- Signature: signed with internal attestation key (KMIP/KMS-backed), include public key thumbprint in metadata.json.
- Checksum: SHA-256 on complete tar.gz recorded in evidence index.

Log slices and linkage:
- For space efficiency, include only audit-log slices relevant to the attestation window and the affected principals. Each log slice must include: timestamp, principal_id, auth_action, resource, outcome, correlation_id.
- Example log query for slice generation (Elasticsearch/KQL):
  GET /_search?size=10000
  { "query": { "bool": { "must": [ { "range": { "@timestamp": { "gte": "2026-07-01T00:00:00Z", "lte": "2026-07-31T23:59:59Z" } } }, { "terms": { "principal_id": ["user:alice", "svc:build-agent"] } } ] } } }

Retention and archival rules (summary):
- Evidence Type: Role membership snapshots | Default Retention: 7 years | Cross-border rule: Keep in region of record; if exported, redact PII | Archive medium: S3 encrypted (KMS-restricted) / on-prem vault
- Evidence Type: Audit log slices | Default Retention: 3 years | Cross-border rule: Preserve full logs where required by customer contract | Archive medium: S3 Glacier Deep/On-prem WORM
- Evidence Type: Attestation manifests | Default Retention: 10 years | Cross-border rule: Follow longest legal hold | Archive medium: S3 immutability + signed manifest
- Evidence Type: Exception tickets | Default Retention: 7 years | Cross-border rule: May be redacted to remove customer data when requested | Archive medium: Encrypted DB export + archive

Note: Where local law requires longer retention (e.g., certain APAC customers), the retention period is extended accordingly. Legal hold supersedes retention (see Legal hold section).

Legal hold and eDiscovery:
- Legal hold is initiated by Compliance/Legal. Once a hold is created, retention clocks pause for affected evidence bundles.
- Playbook step: Compliance tags relevant AEB IDs and notifies archive system to set immutable hold flag.
- Evidence under legal hold can be exported to a sealed container for lawyers only, with strict access logging and multi-party approval.

Exception handling (when attestation fails or anomalous access found):
1) If owner marks access as incorrect or logging shows anomalous behavior, generate an exception ticket in the risk register.
2) Triage: Security (oncall) inspects within 4 hours for Tier 0/1 and 24 hours for Tier 2/3.
3) If immediate risk, require emergency role revocation + heartbeat audits for 7 days.
4) Evidence for exception includes pre/post revocation role snapshots and associated logs; attach to incident for audit.
5) Remediation must include root cause, actions taken, and preventive changes; remediation summary appended to AEB.

Integration with Incident Response and SLO alignment:
- Access-related incidents escalate to security incident response using existing incident channels.
- SLA for attestation processing: 95% of attestation bundles must be generated and archived within 24 hours of final approval.
- Audit log retrieval SLA for audits: initial acknowledgment within 1 business day; full slice delivery within 5 business days for standard customer audits, expedited for contractual needs.

Evidence access controls and query patterns:
- Access to archived AEBs requires role-based approval: only Compliance, Legal, and Security with a valid business justification and MFA.
- All access is logged with a unique correlation_id that appears in the AEB access-trail field.
- Example retrieval flow (high level):
  1) Requester opens evidence request ticket (Jira) and attaches justification.
  2) Compliance owner approves.
  3) Archive system issues time-limited, auditable link and logs retrieval event.

Operational runbook (step-by-step attestation -> archive):
1) IAM snapshot job runs on scheduled cadence, stores raw output in temporary staging bucket for 7 days.
2) Attestation task queue sends batched notifications to role owners.
3) Owners approve/reject via UI.
4) On approval, attestation service packages AEB, signs it, calculates checksum, and writes metadata to Evidence Index (DB).
5) Archive worker copies AEB to configured archival medium, applies immutability policy if required, and tags AEB with retention/region/hold metadata.
6) Evidence Index records archive location and retention window; notifications sent to Compliance.

Operational commands and checks (examples):
- Verify AEB integrity: sha256sum aeb.tar.gz && cat metadata.json | jq .checksum
- List archived bundles by role: redwood-evidence list --role prod-service-ops --since 2024-01-01
- Trigger legal-hold flag: redwood-evidence hold --bundle-id BUNDLE-2026-07-01-12345 --reason "litigation-ACME" --approver legal@redwood.com

Monitoring and KPIs:
- Attestation completion rate by tier (goal: >98% on or before due date).
- Bundle generation SLA (goal: 95% < 24 hours).
- Evidence retrieval SLA (goal: 95% within 5 business days).
- Exceptions re-open rate (goal: <5% after 90 days).

Security controls and cryptography:
- Signing keys stored in KMS with quarterly rotation and M-of-N access for emergency recovery.
- AEBs encrypted with envelope encryption; per-archive KMS key selection based on region.
- Immutable tags applied to archived objects where regulator requires WORM behavior.

Audit readiness checklist (for auditors):
1) Provide Evidence Index export for requested date range (including checksums and signatures).
2) Provide sampled AEBs and log slices with hash chain verifying integrity.
3) Demonstrate attestation workflow and show approver audit trail.
4) Show legal hold flags and their state transitions.

Appendix: Example metadata.json (abridged) - JSON shown with escaped quotes:
{
  "bundle_id": "BUNDLE-2026-07-01-12345",
  "attestation_window": "2026-07-01/2026-07-31",
  "created_by": "attest-service@redwood.com",
  "signature": "kms:sign:projects/redwood/keys/attest-key:signature-b64",
  "checksum": "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb924...",
  "retention_policy": "7y",
  "archive_location": "s3://evidence-prod/2026/07/BUNDLE-2026-07-01-12345.tar.gz",
  "immutable_flag": "true"
}
